run: random phase, SPIRE agent sync_interval and server cache_reload_interval both 1 s, chain P -> C only
headline: revoke_to_deny_ms: P sends DELETE /delegations/{chain_id} (t0) -> C receives its first 403 from the resource for GET /datasets/A, sent with a JWT-SVID C fetched from its agent in the same tick
secondary: revoke_to_identity_gone_ms: t0 -> C receives the answer to its first failed JWT-SVID fetch (PermissionDenied, no identity issued); C does not call the resource when a fetch fails. Also recorded: deny_to_identity_gone_ms (first 403 received -> failed fetch received)
why_403_not_401: a revoked child's JWT-SVID stays cryptographically valid until it expires, so the resource accepts the token and OPA denies it (403); the resource sends 401 only for a missing, malformed, expired or otherwise invalid token. No tokenless call is made, and no 401 is expected or produced.
child_behaviour: C runs `parentsim revoke-wait` in its own pod after the vend, once it holds the vended SVID: every 20 ms it fetches a fresh JWT-SVID (audience spiffe://lab.local/svc/resource) from its SPIRE agent through one long-lived Workload API client and, in the same tick, sends GET /datasets/A with it. It prints ready at its first 200, keeps looping through the 403s, and stops at its first failed token fetch (at most one tick in flight).
harness: src/experiments/revoke_to_deny.py (reusing revocation_speed.py's and vend_to_svid.py's parts), parentsim modes revoke-wait (C) and dispose-timed (P)
reference_instant: P's pod stamps the wall clock (CLOCK_REALTIME, Unix ns) just before it writes the DELETE; all stamps are compared across pods on the single-host kind clock

code.state: uncommitted working tree at run time

command: cd src/experiments && CLUSTER_NAME=nhi-lab KUBECTX=kind-bench-rtd-1s TRUST_DOMAIN=lab.local uv run python3 revoke_to_deny.py --trials 50 --jitter-s 1 --run-id 20261103T044158Z-revoke-to-deny-1s

jitter.applies: a seeded uniform random 0..jitter_s wait after C's ready and before the DELETE, then a 0.2 s settle, so the DELETE lands at a random point of the agent's sync cycle

cluster.kind_cluster: bench-rtd-1s (throwaway, two nodes), created for this run and deleted after it
bring_up: make policy-engine-up vending-service-up resource-up experiments-fixtures-up KIND_CLUSTER=bench-rtd-1s
cluster.note: the runs were started without make, because the make targets re-apply the repository's SPIRE ConfigMaps

config_changes_on_this_cluster_only.change: in the server block of the live spire-server ConfigMap: `audit_log_enabled = true` and `experimental { cache_reload_interval = "1s" }` (default 5 s); StatefulSet restarted
in the agent block of the live spire-agent ConfigMap: `experimental { sync_interval = "1s" }` (default 5 s); DaemonSet restarted after the server

smoke_run: 2 trials with --jitter-s 1 passed (both ok, every cross-check populated except the agent log line, which is empty by nature) before the 50-trial run, on the same cluster and config; its output is not kept
cross_checks_not_populated: agent_log_*: C's node agent logs nothing that names C's ID after the DELETE at its INFO level (it logs the entry's creation only), so the column is empty in every trial

logs.window: contiguous per trial: from the end of the previous trial's window (the first starts 1 s before trial 1) to the moment C held no identity again after the revoke
logs.timestamp: first field of each line: the container runtime's capture time (kubectl logs --timestamps); for parent/, the time this host received P's command output; spire-agent/ is C's node agent
